# fastweb.com API

Browse and search scholarships by category, state, or major from Fastweb.com. Get detailed scholarship information, financial aid articles, and student discounts.

## Install / import

```python
from parse_apis.fastweb_com_api import Fastweb
```

## Operations

Call these on the client's collection accessors (e.g. `client.<collection>.<op>(…)`) or via active-record navigation on returned objects — see [`example.py`](./example.py) for the exact call spelling. List operations return a lazy `Paginator`.

| Call | Returns | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `client.articles.list(limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Article]` | Returns recent financial aid articles from Fastweb covering topics like FAFSA, student loans, financial aid strategies, and loan forgiveness programs. No input parameters required. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.categories.list(limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Category]` | Returns all browseable scholarship categories from the Fastweb directory page. Each category includes a name, slug, and URL. Use the slug with get_scholarships_by_category to retrieve scholarships in that category. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.discounts.list(limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Discount]` | Returns available student discounts and deals from various merchants partnered with Fastweb. Each discount includes the merchant name and the offer description. No input parameters required. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.scholarships.by_major(major: Major \| Literal['Biology', 'Nursing', 'Business', 'Engineering', 'Computer Science'], limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Scholarship]` | Returns scholarships for a specific academic major or field of study. Constructs the directory slug from the major name (e.g. 'Engineering' becomes 'scholarships-for-engineering-majors'). Each scholarship includes title, provider, award amount, deadline, and detail_url. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.scholarships.by_state(state: State \| Literal['Texas', 'Florida', 'Illinois', 'New York', 'California'], limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Scholarship]` | Returns scholarships specific to a U.S. state. Constructs the directory slug from the state name (e.g. 'California' becomes 'california-scholarships'). Each scholarship includes title, provider, award amount, deadline, and detail_url. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.scholarships.featured(limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Scholarship]` | Returns currently featured and promoted scholarship opportunities from Fastweb's homepage. These are frequently updated sponsored listings. No input parameters required. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.scholarships.by_category(slug: str, limit: Optional[int] = None, max_fetches: int = 1000)` | `Paginator[Scholarship]` | Returns scholarships for a specific category from the Fastweb directory. Accepts a category slug (obtainable from get_scholarship_directory_categories). Each scholarship includes title, provider, award amount, deadline, and a detail_url for use with get_scholarship_detail. Single-fetch result set; the iterator yields one page. |
| `client.scholarship_details.get(id_slug: str)` | `ScholarshipDetail` | Returns comprehensive details for a specific scholarship including full description, award amount, deadline, awards available, and provider. The id_slug is the final path segment from a scholarship's detail_url (e.g. '77822-women-s-league-scholarship-uiuc'). |

## Errors

| Error | Raised when | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| `CategoryNotFound` | The category slug does not exist on Fastweb (404/410 response) | `slug` |

Runtime errors (`RateLimitError`, `UpstreamError`, `PaginationLimitError`, …) are importable from `parse_apis` and can occur on any call.

> **Note.** Some params accept an enum whose corresponding output field is raw `str`/`list` (the wire value isn't bound to the enum). Enum members never compare equal to raw strings — compare such output values against `member.value`, or use plain string literals.
